text: An ML engineer is collecting data to train a classification ML model by using Amazon SageMaker AI. The target column can have two possible values: Class A or Class B. The ML engineer wants to ensure that the number of samples for both Class A and Class B are balanced, without losing any existing training data. The ML engineer must test the balance of the training data. Which solution will meet this requirement?

choices.A: Use SageMaker Clarify to check for class imbalance (CI). If the value is equal to 0, then use random undersampling in SageMaker Data Wrangler to balance the classes.
choices.B: Use SageMaker Clarify to check for class imbalance (CI). If the value is greater than 0, then use synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Data Wrangler to balance the classes.
choices.C: Use SageMaker JumpStart to generate a class imbalance (CI) report. If the value is greater than 0, then use random undersampling in SageMaker Studio to balance the classes.
choices.D: Use SageMaker JumpStart to generate a class imbalance (CI) report. If the value is equal to 0, then use synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Studio to balance the classes.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The ML engineer must test the balance of the training data. Which solution will meet this requirement?
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Oversampling can balance training classes without deleting original records. A signed imbalance measure depends on which category is assigned to each comparison group.

A. Use SageMaker Clarify to check for class imbalance (CI). If the value is equal to 0, then use random undersampling in SageMaker Data Wrangler to balance the classes. — A zero imbalance value indicates equal group counts, so rebalancing is unnecessary. Undersampling also discards existing records, violating the requirement.

B. Use SageMaker Clarify to check for class imbalance (CI). If the value is greater than 0, then use synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Data Wrangler to balance the classes. — When the configured positive imbalance indicates a majority group, SMOTE can add minority-class training examples without dropping originals. Inspect both signs of imbalance, and apply resampling only to the training partition with an appropriate feature representation.

C. Use SageMaker JumpStart to generate a class imbalance (CI) report. If the value is greater than 0, then use random undersampling in SageMaker Studio to balance the classes. — JumpStart is not the bias-reporting tool described, and undersampling removes original data.

D. Use SageMaker JumpStart to generate a class imbalance (CI) report. If the value is equal to 0, then use synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Studio to balance the classes. — JumpStart is not the specified imbalance analysis tool, and a zero imbalance value does not justify oversampling.

text: An ML engineer is building a logistic regression model to predict customer churn for subscription services. The ML engineer is using a dataset that contains two string variables: location and job_seniority_level. The location variable has 3 distinct values, and the job_seniority_level variable has over 10 distinct values. The ML engineer must perform preprocessing on the variables. Which solution will meet this requirement?

choices.A: Apply tokenization to location. Apply ordinal encoding to job_seniority_level.
choices.B: Apply one-hot encoding to location. Apply ordinal encoding to job_seniority_level
choices.C: Apply binning to location. Apply standard scaling to job_seniority_level.
choices.D: Apply one-hot encoding to location. Apply standard scaling to job_seniority_level.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The ML engineer must perform preprocessing on the variables. Which solution will meet this requirement?

explanation:
Key Concept: Nominal categories need an encoding without artificial order. An ordinal category can use an explicit rank when that order has meaning.

A. Apply tokenization to location. Apply ordinal encoding to job_seniority_level. — Tokenizing a three-valued location field treats a structured category as free text and adds unnecessary complexity.

B. Apply one-hot encoding to location. Apply ordinal encoding to job_seniority_level — Use one-hot indicators for location and an explicit seniority rank for job level. In logistic regression, validate the implied relationship between rank increments and log odds; use a richer encoding if it is not appropriate.

C. Apply binning to location. Apply standard scaling to job_seniority_level. — Binning is mainly for continuous values, and standard scaling cannot directly process the string job-level categories.

D. Apply one-hot encoding to location. Apply standard scaling to job_seniority_level. — One-hot encoding is suitable for location, but job seniority strings must be encoded before numerical standard scaling can be applied.

text: A company needs to deploy a custom-trained classification ML model on AWS. The model must make near real-time predictions with low latency and must handle variable request volumes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create an Amazon SageMaker AI batch transform job to process inference requests in batches.
choices.B: Use Amazon API Gateway to receive prediction requests. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to host and serve the model.
choices.C: Deploy an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint. Configure auto scaling for the endpoint.
choices.D: Launch AWS Deep Learning AMIs (DLAMI) on two Amazon EC2 instances. Run the instances behind an Application Load Balancer.

hint:

explanation:
Key Concept: A managed real-time endpoint with auto scaling supports synchronous low-latency inference while adapting provisioned capacity to demand.

A. Create an Amazon SageMaker AI batch transform job to process inference requests in batches. — Batch transform processes offline batches rather than responding to individual near-real-time requests.

B. Use Amazon API Gateway to receive prediction requests. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to host and serve the model. — S3 stores model artifacts but does not execute model code to serve predictions.

C. Deploy an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint. Configure auto scaling for the endpoint. — Deploy the model to a real-time SageMaker endpoint and configure capacity limits, target tracking, and suitable warm capacity for the latency requirement.

D. Launch AWS Deep Learning AMIs (DLAMI) on two Amazon EC2 instances. Run the instances behind an Application Load Balancer. — Two fixed EC2 instances behind a load balancer do not automatically scale for varying request volumes and require more serving infrastructure management.

text: A company runs a neural network model and retrains the model when the performance degrades. The company uses a training job that uses Amazon SageMaker AI distributed data parallelism (DDP). The training job takes several hours to run. The company wants to decrease the required time for the training job. Which solution will meet this requirement?

choices.A: Increase the number of epochs.
choices.B: Increase the number of neurons in the hidden layers.
choices.C: Increase the number of layers.
choices.D: Increase the number of instances.

explanation:
Key Concept: Distributed data parallelism divides training batches across workers and synchronizes gradients. Additional instances can reduce elapsed time when computation scales efficiently.

A. Increase the number of epochs. — More epochs perform more passes over the dataset and generally increase training time.

B. Increase the number of neurons in the hidden layers. — More hidden neurons increase computation and memory use rather than reducing the work of the existing model.

C. Increase the number of layers. — Additional layers increase model computation and can make each training step slower.

D. Increase the number of instances. — Increase the number of compatible instances so more training examples are processed in parallel. Benchmark communication overhead, global batch size, convergence, and cost because speedup is not guaranteed to be linear.

text: An ML engineer decides to use Amazon SageMaker AI automated model tuning (AMT) for hyperparameter optimization (HPO). The strategy must work across small hyperparameter ranges. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Grid search
choices.B: Random search
choices.C: Bayesian optimization
choices.D: Hyperband

explanation:
Key Concept: Bayesian optimization builds a surrogate model of objective performance and uses previous trials to choose promising next hyperparameters.

A. Grid search — Grid search follows a predefined combination grid instead of adapting to previous results through a surrogate model.

B. Random search — Random search samples independently and does not use previous objective values to guide the next choice.

C. Bayesian optimization — Bayesian optimization uses a probabilistic regression model and acquisition strategy to choose subsequent trials, matching the sequential, informed search described.

D. Hyperband — Hyperband allocates budgets to configurations and stops poor trials early. Its defining mechanism is successive resource allocation rather than regression-guided sequential selection.

text: A healthcare company wants to detect irregularities in patient vital signs that could indicate early signs of a medical condition. The company has an unlabeled dataset that includes patient health records, medication history, and lifestyle changes. Which algorithm and hyperparameter should the company use to meet this requirement?

choices.A: Use the Amazon SageMaker AI XGBoost algorithm. Set max_depth to greater than 100 to regulate tree complexity.
choices.B: Use the Amazon SageMaker AI k-means clustering algorithm. Set k to determine the number of clusters.
choices.C: Use the Amazon SageMaker AI DeepAR algorithm. Set epochs to the number of training iterations.
choices.D: Use the Amazon SageMaker AI Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm. Set num_trees to greater than 100.

explanation:
Key Concept: Random Cut Forest assigns anomaly scores to unlabeled numerical feature vectors. Ensemble size controls a tradeoff between score stability and computation.

A. Use the Amazon SageMaker AI XGBoost algorithm. Set max_depth to greater than 100 to regulate tree complexity. — Supervised XGBoost needs a target for this classification framing. Setting tree depth above 100 would not solve missing labels and can greatly increase complexity.

B. Use the Amazon SageMaker AI k-means clustering algorithm. Set k to determine the number of clusters. — K-means can support distance-based anomaly heuristics, but it is not the built-in anomaly scoring algorithm most directly suited to the stated task.

C. Use the Amazon SageMaker AI DeepAR algorithm. Set epochs to the number of training iterations. — DeepAR is a time-series forecasting algorithm. The question does not define the forecasting target and time-series structure needed for it.

D. Use the Amazon SageMaker AI Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm. Set num_trees to greater than 100. — RCF is designed for unsupervised anomaly detection. More than 100 trees can form a larger ensemble, but that threshold is not a universal accuracy guarantee; validate tree count and preprocessing on the application.

text: An ML engineer at an entertainment company is refining an ML model to predict audience preferences. As the model learns from data, the ML engineer notices that the model’s performance peaks early and then begins to gradually decline. The ML engineer must prevent the performance degradation after initial success. Which solution will meet this requirement?

choices.A: Increase the number of layers.
choices.B: Implement early stopping.
choices.C: Add more neurons to each layer to capture complex patterns.
choices.D: Examine model bias and variance to understand performance issues.

explanation:
Key Concept: Early stopping halts training when held-out performance stops improving and can restore the best checkpoint before overfitting grows.

A. Increase the number of layers. — Additional layers increase capacity and can worsen the later-stage overfitting behavior.

B. Implement early stopping. — Monitor an appropriate validation metric, stop after a defined patience interval without improvement, and retain the best model checkpoint.

C. Add more neurons to each layer to capture complex patterns. — Adding neurons increases capacity rather than preventing training from continuing past the best generalization point.

D. Examine model bias and variance to understand performance issues. — Bias/variance analysis can diagnose the cause, but analysis alone does not stop the degrading training process.

text: An ML engineer is tuning an image classification model that shows poor performance on one of two available classes during prediction. Analysis reveals that the images whose class the model performed poorly on represent an extremely small fraction of the whole training dataset. The ML engineer must improve the model’s performance. Which solution will meet this requirement?

choices.A: Optimize for accuracy. Use image augmentation on the less common images to generate new samples.
choices.B: Optimize for F1 score. Use image augmentation on the less common images to generate new samples.
choices.C: Optimize for accuracy. Use Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the less common images to generate new samples.
choices.D: Optimize for F1 score. Use Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the less common images to generate new samples.

hint:

explanation:
Key Concept: Imbalanced image classification benefits from minority-class-aware evaluation and realistic, label-preserving image augmentation.

A. Optimize for accuracy. Use image augmentation on the less common images to generate new samples. — Minority augmentation is appropriate, but overall accuracy can remain high even when the minority class is largely missed.

B. Optimize for F1 score. Use image augmentation on the less common images to generate new samples. — Use a minority-class or macro F1 objective and augment minority images with valid transformations. Evaluate on untouched held-out data with the natural class distribution.

C. Optimize for accuracy. Use Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the less common images to generate new samples. — Accuracy can hide minority failure, and ordinary SMOTE on raw image pixels can create unrealistic images that do not preserve meaningful visual structure.

D. Optimize for F1 score. Use Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the less common images to generate new samples. — F1 is suitable, but direct pixel-space SMOTE is usually less appropriate than label-preserving image transformations. SMOTE in a validated embedding space would be a different, explicitly designed method.

The dataset includes fields for month, sales region, regional aggregate sales, and the number of stores in each sales region. The company notices that during two months of every year, the aggregate sales values are unexpectedly high. The company performs one-hot encoding on all non-numerical features in the training and validation datasets. The company uses the training dataset to train the classification model. When the company evaluates the model against the validation dataset, the results are less accurate than expected. The company must improve the model’s accuracy on the validation dataset. Which solution will meet this requirement?

choices.A: Remove records that include outliers across all features.
choices.B: Use a stratified split on the month and sales region features.
choices.C: Perform normalization on the aggregate sales feature.
choices.D: Perform normalization on the aggregate sales feature for each sales region.

Perform normalization on the aggregate sales feature for each sales region. — Per-region normalization can reduce regional scale differences, but cannot be assumed to fix seasonal peaks or the unspecified model. The source's definitive claim needs more information about the target, algorithm, and split.

text: A company is creating an ML model to identify defects in a product. The company has gathered a dataset and has stored the dataset in TIFF format in Amazon S3. The dataset contains 200 images in which the most common defects are visible. The dataset also contains 1,800 images in which there is no defect visible. An ML engineer trains the model and notices poor performance in some classes. The ML engineer identifies a class imbalance problem in the dataset. What should the ML engineer do to solves this problem?

choices.A: Use a few hundred images and Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to train a new model.
choices.B: Undersample the 200 images in which the most common defects are visible.
choices.C: Oversample the 200 images in which the most common defects are visible.
choices.D: Use all 2,000 images and Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to train a new model.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The ML engineer identifies a class imbalance problem in the dataset. What should the ML engineer do to solves this problem?
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: class imbalance
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: The defect class is the minority: 200 defect images versus 1,800 non-defect images. Rebalancing should increase minority representation or reduce the majority, not shrink the minority.

A. Use a few hundred images and Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to train a new model. — Changing to a managed service and an arbitrary smaller dataset does not specifically address the identified imbalance.

B. Undersample the 200 images in which the most common defects are visible. — Removing some of the 200 defect images makes the minority representation even smaller and can discard useful defect diversity.

C. Oversample the 200 images in which the most common defects are visible. — Oversample the defect training images, preferably with valid augmentation where appropriate. Keep evaluation images separate to avoid leakage from duplicated examples.

D. Use all 2,000 images and Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to train a new model. — Using the same imbalanced dataset with a different service does not by itself rebalance the classes.

text: A company is developing an application that reads animal descriptions from user prompts and generates images based on the information from the prompts. The application reads a message from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Then the application uses Amazon Titan Image Generator on Amazon Bedrock to generate an image based on the information in the message. Finally, the application removes the message from SQS queue. Which IAM permissions should the company assign to the application’s IAM role? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Allow the bedrock:InvokeModel action for the Amazon Titan Image Generator resource.
choices.B: Allow the bedrock:Get* action for the Amazon Titan Image Generator resource.
choices.C: Allow the sqs:ReceiveMessage action and the sqs:DeleteMessage action for the SQS queue resource.
choices.D: Allow the sqs:GetQueueAttributes action and the sqs:DeleteMessage action for the SQS queue resource.
choices.E: Allow the sagemaker:PutRecord* action for the Amazon Titan Image Generator resource.

hint:

explanation:
Key Concept: Least-privilege permissions should match each application action: receive work, invoke the image model, and delete completed work.

A. Allow the bedrock:InvokeModel action for the Amazon Titan Image Generator resource. — bedrock:InvokeModel authorizes generating an image with the specified model resource through the runtime API.

B. Allow the bedrock:Get* action for the Amazon Titan Image Generator resource. — Get operations read metadata or configuration. They do not authorize a model inference invocation.

C. Allow the sqs:ReceiveMessage action and the sqs:DeleteMessage action for the SQS queue resource. — sqs:ReceiveMessage reads a queued task, and sqs:DeleteMessage removes it after successful processing. Scope both permissions to the intended queue.

D. Allow the sqs:GetQueueAttributes action and the sqs:DeleteMessage action for the SQS queue resource. — GetQueueAttributes reads queue configuration, not message contents. ReceiveMessage is still required to obtain the task.

E. Allow the sagemaker:PutRecord* action for the Amazon Titan Image Generator resource. — SageMaker PutRecord actions concern Feature Store ingestion, not Bedrock image generation.

text: A company is developing an ML model to forecast future values based on time series data. The dataset includes historical measurements collected at regular intervals and categorical features. The model needs to predict future values based on past patterns and trends. Which algorithm and hyperparameters should the company use to develop the model?

choices.A: Use the Amazon SageMaker AI XGBoost algorithm. Set the scale_pos_weight hyperparameter to adjust for class imbalance.
choices.B: Use k-means clustering with k to specify the number of clusters.
choices.C: Use the Amazon SageMaker AI DeepAR algorithm with matching context_length and prediction_length hyperparameters.
choices.D: Use the Amazon SageMaker AI Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm with contamination to set the expected proportion of anomalies.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The model needs to predict future values based on past patterns and trends. Which algorithm and hyperparameters should the company use to develop the model?

explanation:
Key Concept: DeepAR learns shared temporal patterns across related numerical time series and can condition forecasts on categorical features.

A. Use the Amazon SageMaker AI XGBoost algorithm. Set the scale_pos_weight hyperparameter to adjust for class imbalance. — scale_pos_weight addresses binary class imbalance in XGBoost, not the time-series context and forecast horizon described.

B. Use k-means clustering with k to specify the number of clusters. — K-means clusters observations. It does not model the ordered history needed to forecast future numerical values.

C. Use the Amazon SageMaker AI DeepAR algorithm with matching context_length and prediction_length hyperparameters. — DeepAR is the appropriate forecasting algorithm. Starting with context_length similar to prediction_length is a tuning heuristic, not a mandatory equality; choose both based on the horizon and validation results.

D. Use the Amazon SageMaker AI Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm with contamination to set the expected proportion of anomalies. — RCF detects anomalies rather than forecasting the future target sequence. contamination is not the stated SageMaker built-in RCF hyperparameter.

text: An ML engineer is designing an AI-powered traffic management system to adjust traffic lights during predicted congestion. The system must use near real-time inference to generate predictions to help prevent traffic collisions. The system must use a batch processing pipeline to perform historical analysis of the predictions to continuously refine and improve the model. The historical analysis will take several hours to evaluate how well the predictions correlate with actual outcomes. The system must be able to scale inference endpoints appropriately to meet demand. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Use Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoints. Configure the endpoints to scale automatically based on a target tracking scaling policy that uses the metric ConcurrentInvocationsPerinstance.
choices.B: Configure reserved concurrency for AWS Lambda functions to process streaming data. Use Lambda SnapStart to connect the Lambda functions to Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoints to support near real-time traffic predictions.
choices.C: Configure an Amazon SageMaker Processing job for batch analysis of historical prediction data. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule the job to run daily. Allow several hours for in-depth analysis to refine and improve the traffic management model.
choices.D: Use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to host containers to support the batch analysis of historical prediction data. Configure scaling based on Amazon CloudWatch metrics to analyze historical traffic patterns and model performance over multiple hours.
choices.E: Use an AWS Lambda function to perform the historical analysis. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: real-time, near real-time, batch
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Use synchronous managed inference for immediate predictions and a separate long-running processing job for historical evaluation. Scaling must reference a supported metric.

A. Use Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoints. Configure the endpoints to scale automatically based on a target tracking scaling policy that uses the metric ConcurrentInvocationsPerinstance. — Real-time endpoints with target tracking fit the online workload, but ConcurrentInvocationsPerinstance is not the documented metric name. Use a supported metric such as InvocationsPerInstance or the high-resolution ConcurrentRequestsPerModel.

B. Configure reserved concurrency for AWS Lambda functions to process streaming data. Use Lambda SnapStart to connect the Lambda functions to Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoints to support near real-time traffic predictions. — Reserved concurrency limits Lambda execution capacity, and SnapStart reduces supported Lambda startup time. It is not a connector to SageMaker or the endpoint's scaling policy.

C. Configure an Amazon SageMaker Processing job for batch analysis of historical prediction data. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule the job to run daily. Allow several hours for in-depth analysis to refine and improve the traffic management model. — A scheduled SageMaker Processing job can run the multi-hour historical analysis and compare predictions with actual outcomes without tying up online serving capacity.

D. Use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to host containers to support the batch analysis of historical prediction data. Configure scaling based on Amazon CloudWatch metrics to analyze historical traffic patterns and model performance over multiple hours. — An EC2 Auto Scaling group can run custom analysis workers, but needs explicit batch orchestration and host management. It is not necessary when Processing provides the managed job runtime.

E. Use an AWS Lambda function to perform the historical analysis. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function. — A single Lambda invocation is limited to 15 minutes, which is shorter than the several-hour analysis. The intended A/C pair requires correcting A's metric name.
notes: Source selects A and C. The real-time plus Processing architecture fits, but A names ConcurrentInvocationsPerinstance instead of a supported documented metric. Correct the metric before treating the combination as deployable.

analysis.keyConcept: Use synchronous managed inference for immediate predictions and a separate long-running processing job for historical evaluation. Scaling must reference a supported metric.

options.A: Real-time endpoints with target tracking fit the online workload, but ConcurrentInvocationsPerinstance is not the documented metric name. Use a supported metric such as InvocationsPerInstance or the high-resolution ConcurrentRequestsPerModel.
options.B: Reserved concurrency limits Lambda execution capacity, and SnapStart reduces supported Lambda startup time. It is not a connector to SageMaker or the endpoint's scaling policy.
options.C: A scheduled SageMaker Processing job can run the multi-hour historical analysis and compare predictions with actual outcomes without tying up online serving capacity.
options.D: An EC2 Auto Scaling group can run custom analysis workers, but needs explicit batch orchestration and host management. It is not necessary when Processing provides the managed job runtime.
options.E: A single Lambda invocation is limited to 15 minutes, which is shorter than the several-hour analysis. The intended A/C pair requires correcting A's metric name.

text: A company wants to launch a new website feature that predicts home prices based on user-supplied home attributes. The attributes include location, square footage, and number of bedrooms and bathrooms. An ML engineer has trained a regression model by using the Amazon SageMaker AI XGBoost algorithm. The model performs well with training data. However, the model significantly underperforms when it is validated against real-world data. Which solution will improve the model’s validation score with the LEAST implementation effort?

choices.A: Create a larger training dataset that includes more real-world data. Retrain the model.
choices.B: Increase the value of the num_round hyperparameter.
choices.C: Change the eval_metric hyperparameter from Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) to Error.
choices.D: Increase the value of the lambda hyperparameter.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: However, the model significantly underperforms when it is validated against real-world data. Which solution will improve the model’s validation score with the LEAST implementation effort?
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: LEAST
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Strong training performance with weak validation performance suggests overfitting or a distribution mismatch. XGBoost's lambda parameter adds L2 regularization to make fitting more conservative.

A. Create a larger training dataset that includes more real-world data. Retrain the model. — More representative data can help if the training population is inadequate, but collecting and preparing it generally takes more effort than tuning an existing regularization parameter.

B. Increase the value of the num_round hyperparameter. — Increasing boosting rounds can fit the training set more closely and worsen overfitting unless controlled by validation and early stopping.

C. Change the eval_metric hyperparameter from Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) to Error. — Error is a classification evaluation metric and is inappropriate for this continuous house-price regression task. Changing a metric alone does not improve predictions.

D. Increase the value of the lambda hyperparameter. — Increase and validate lambda to penalize excessive weight magnitudes and reduce overfitting. This is the least-effort targeted change among the choices; confirmed data distribution mismatch would additionally require representative data.

notes: Corrected source key A to D. For the described training/validation gap, increasing XGBoost lambda adds L2 regularization with less implementation effort than acquiring a larger dataset. Validate the setting; confirmed distribution shift would also require representative data.

text: A company is performing A/B testing on a model that provides product recommendations. The company has deployed two versions of the model and is showing each version of the model to 50% of users randomly. Which metric should the company use to evaluate whether users act on a recommendation?

choices.A: The conversion rates between the two versions of the model
choices.B: The number of recommendations provided to each user
choices.C: The model accuracy on held-out test data
choices.D: The latency of model inference

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The company has deployed two versions of the model and is showing each version of the model to 50% of users randomly. Which metric should the company use to evaluate whether users act on a recommendation?
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Online recommendation experiments should measure the user action the product aims to cause, such as a purchase or another defined conversion.

A. The conversion rates between the two versions of the model — Compare conversion rates between randomly assigned groups, using a consistent attribution window and statistical uncertainty. This directly measures whether users act on recommendations.

B. The number of recommendations provided to each user — Recommendation count measures exposure, not whether the user followed or acted on the recommendation.

C. The model accuracy on held-out test data — Offline test accuracy can be useful, but does not directly measure user behavior in the live randomized experiment.

D. The latency of model inference — Inference latency affects experience but is an operational metric rather than the requested action outcome.

text: A company is using Amazon SageMaker AI to build an ML model to predict customer behavior. The company needs to explain the bias in the model to an auditor. The explanation must focus on demographics data of the customers. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use SageMaker Clarify to generate a bias report. Send the report to the auditor.
choices.B: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to create a job to detect drift in the model's data quality. Send the job output to the auditor.
choices.C: Use Amazon Quick Suite (previously known as Amazon QuickSight) integration with SageMaker AI to generate a bias report from Quick Suite. Send the report to the auditor.
choices.D: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics from the SageMaker AI namespace to create a bias dashboard. Share the dashboard with the auditor.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The explanation must focus on demographics data of the customers. Which solution will meet these requirements?
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: A demographic bias report compares outcomes across specified sensitive groups and documents the selected fairness metrics and evaluation data.

A. Use SageMaker Clarify to generate a bias report. Send the report to the auditor. — Configure Clarify with the demographic facets and relevant labels or predictions, generate the bias report, and provide its assumptions and interpretation to the auditor.

B. Use AWS Glue DataBrew to create a job to detect drift in the model's data quality. Send the job output to the auditor. — Data-quality drift concerns changes in inputs. It is not a demographic fairness assessment of the model.

C. Use Amazon Quick Suite (previously known as Amazon QuickSight) integration with SageMaker AI to generate a bias report from Quick Suite. Send the report to the auditor. — A dashboard tool can display computed metrics but does not automatically generate the required bias analysis merely through a SageMaker integration.

D. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics from the SageMaker AI namespace to create a bias dashboard. Share the dashboard with the auditor. — Default endpoint CloudWatch metrics measure serving behavior. They do not establish demographic bias without a configured bias monitoring or analysis job.
notes: Service availability: SageMaker Clarify is closed to new customers; existing customers can continue using it. This answer describes its documented capabilities.

text: A digital media entertainment company needs real-time video content moderation to ensure compliance during live streaming events. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Use Amazon Rekognition and AWS Lambda to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames.
choices.B: Use Amazon Rekognition and a large language model (LLM) hosted on Amazon Bedrock to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames.
choices.C: Use Amazon SageMaker AI to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames.
choices.D: Use Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Comprehend to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: A digital media entertainment company needs real-time video content moderation to ensure compliance during live streaming events. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: LEAST operational overhead, real-time, LEAST
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Managed image moderation can analyze sampled frames from a live video pipeline. The application must define frame extraction, latency, and coverage requirements.

A. Use Amazon Rekognition and AWS Lambda to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames. — Extract suitable frames and use Rekognition moderation APIs through a Lambda-driven workflow. This avoids training and operating a custom moderation model, while sampling and throughput must be sized for the stream.

B. Use Amazon Rekognition and a large language model (LLM) hosted on Amazon Bedrock to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames. — Adding a Bedrock LLM introduces extra inference and integration when Rekognition's moderation labels meet the stated need.

C. Use Amazon SageMaker AI to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames. — A custom SageMaker vision model requires training data, model evaluation, hosting, and maintenance beyond the managed moderation workflow.

D. Use Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Comprehend to extract and analyze the metadata from the videos’ image frames. — Transcribe analyzes audio and Comprehend analyzes text. They do not inspect the visual content of video frames.

text: An ML engineer uses A/B testing to dynamically select recommendation models. The models are deployed on Amazon SageMaker AI endpoints. The ML engineer needs to monitor system metrics such as latency, call volume, and HTTP status codes when the endpoints are invoked. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Use AWS X-Ray tracing to monitor SageMaker AI endpoints.
choices.B: Configure Amazon CloudWatch dashboards with AWS Lambda log processors.
choices.C: Enable AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Access Analyzer to track SageMaker AI endpoint metrics.
choices.D: Deploy AWS Trusted Advisor checks on SageMaker AI endpoint instances.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The ML engineer needs to monitor system metrics such as latency, call volume, and HTTP status codes when the endpoints are invoked. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

explanation:
Key Concept: CloudWatch exposes SageMaker endpoint invocation, latency, and error metrics. Logs can supply additional application details when needed.

A. Use AWS X-Ray tracing to monitor SageMaker AI endpoints. — X-Ray is useful for tracing instrumented application paths, but it is not the simplest source for the endpoint's existing system metrics.

B. Configure Amazon CloudWatch dashboards with AWS Lambda log processors. — Use CloudWatch endpoint metrics and dashboards for latency, volume, and error classes. text: An ML engineer is importing a custom model from the Hugging Face Hub into Amazon Bedrock. The ML engineer wants to use the model with the Amazon Bedrock API in an agentic AI application. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Import the model for deployment by using Amazon Bedrock On-Demand mode.
choices.B: Convert the model to a quantized format. Import the quantized model after conversion.
choices.C: Import the model directly by using the Amazon SageMaker AI SDK in the agentic AI application.
choices.D: During the model import process, configure an auto-scaling policy before using the model in the agentic AI application.
choices.E: In the import job, provide the complete Amazon S3 URI that points to the Hugging Face model files. Ensure that the S3 URI is in the same AWS account as the Amazon Bedrock import job.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Bedrock Custom Model Import accepts supported model architectures and required Hugging Face artifacts, then exposes managed on-demand inference.

A. Import the model for deployment by using Amazon Bedrock On-Demand mode. — Use the imported model's supported on-demand runtime invocation path. The application can incorporate those calls into its agent logic; verify the model's supported APIs and capabilities.

B. Convert the model to a quantized format. Import the quantized model after conversion. — Quantization is not a universal prerequisite and an arbitrary quantized format may not meet the import requirements. Supply the documented supported weights and configuration.

C. Import the model directly by using the Amazon SageMaker AI SDK in the agentic AI application. — The application must create a Bedrock import job through an appropriate Bedrock API or console workflow. Merely using the SageMaker SDK does not import a Hugging Face model into Bedrock.

D. During the model import process, configure an auto-scaling policy before using the model in the agentic AI application. — A customer-configured SageMaker-style auto scaling policy is not required during Bedrock import. Bedrock manages the imported model's serving capacity.

E. In the import job, provide the complete Amazon S3 URI that points to the Hugging Face model files. Ensure that the S3 URI is in the same AWS account as the Amazon Bedrock import job. — Provide the S3 location containing all required supported model files and grant the import role access. A same-account bucket works, although current Bedrock documentation also permits properly authorized cross-account S3 sources.

text: A company is developing ML models by using PyTorch and TensorFlow estimators with Amazon SageMaker AI. An ML engineer configures the SageMaker AI estimator and now needs to initiate a training job that uses a training dataset. Which SageMaker AI SDK method can initiate the training job?

text: An ML engineer used Amazon SageMaker Studio to train a neural network. The neural network logs its information into TensorBoard and uses stochastic gradient descent (SGD) as the optimizer. The ML engineer reviewed training graphs and discovered that the accuracy was not increasing and the loss was decreasing very slowly. The ML engineer needs to improve the model’s performance without increasing the total training time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Increase the initial learning rate.
choices.B: Decrease the initial learning rate.
choices.C: Increase the total number of epochs.
choices.D: Decrease the total number of epochs.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The ML engineer needs to improve the model’s performance without increasing the total training time. Which solution will meet these requirements?
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: An overly small learning rate can make SGD progress too slowly within a fixed training budget. Increasing it cautiously can speed optimization when loss is stable rather than oscillating.

A. Increase the initial learning rate. — Try a larger initial learning rate and evaluate the training and validation curves. It can accelerate the slow, stable optimization described, though an excessive increase would cause instability.

B. Decrease the initial learning rate. — A smaller learning rate makes already small updates even smaller and can slow progress further.

C. Increase the total number of epochs. — More epochs increase the training budget, contrary to the requirement to avoid increasing total training time.

D. Decrease the total number of epochs. — Fewer epochs stop training earlier without fixing the slow progress per update and may worsen underfitting.

text: A company wants to use large language models (LLMs) that are supported by Amazon Bedrock to develop a chat interface for the company’s internal technical documentation. The company stores the documentation as dozens of text files that are several megabytes in total size. The company updates the text files often. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.A: Create a new LLM on Amazon Bedrock. Train the new LLM on the original dataset and the company documentation. Make the new model available in Bedrock for calls from the chat interface.
choices.B: Integrate the company documentation with Amazon Bedrock guardrails. Invoke the guardrails for all Amazon Bedrock calls from the chat interface.
choices.C: Use all the text files to fine tune a model in Amazon Bedrock. Use the fine-tuned model to process user prompts.
choices.D: Upload all the text files to an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. Use the knowledge base to provide context when the chat interface makes calls to Amazon Bedrock.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The company updates the text files often. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: MOST cost-effective, MOST
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: RAG retrieves current documentation at inference time, allowing knowledge updates without repeatedly modifying a model's weights.

A. Create a new LLM on Amazon Bedrock. Train the new LLM on the original dataset and the company documentation. Make the new model available in Bedrock for calls from the chat interface. — Training a new foundation model requires substantial data, compute, and development, far beyond the small internal document collection.

B. Integrate the company documentation with Amazon Bedrock guardrails. Invoke the guardrails for all Amazon Bedrock calls from the chat interface. — Guardrails evaluate or constrain content. They are not a knowledge ingestion and document retrieval system.

C. Use all the text files to fine tune a model in Amazon Bedrock. Use the fine-tuned model to process user prompts. — Fine-tuning is not a reliable replacement for retrieving frequently updated factual documents and would require repeated model updates.

D. Upload all the text files to an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. Use the knowledge base to provide context when the chat interface makes calls to Amazon Bedrock. — Connect the documentation to a Bedrock knowledge base, synchronize updates, and retrieve relevant passages for each question. This supplies current context without retraining the LLM for every document change.

text: A company uses an ML model to recommend videos to users. The model is deployed on Amazon SageMaker AI. The model performed well initially after deployment, but the model’s performance has degraded over time. Which solution can the company use to identify model drift in the future?

choices.A: Create a monitoring job in SageMaker Model Monitor. Then create a baseline from the training dataset.
choices.B: Create a baseline from the training dataset. Then create a monitoring job in SageMaker Model Monitor.
choices.C: Create a baseline by using a built-in rule in SageMaker Clarify. Monitor the drift in Amazon CloudWatch.
choices.D: Retrain the model on new data. Compare the retrained model's performance to the original model’s performance.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The model performed well initially after deployment, but the model’s performance has degraded over time. Which solution can the company use to identify model drift in the future?
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Drift monitoring needs a reference baseline before scheduled comparisons can identify deviations from that reference.

A. Create a monitoring job in SageMaker Model Monitor. Then create a baseline from the training dataset. — The monitoring job must be configured with the intended baseline; creating the comparison workflow first does not establish what constitutes drift.

B. Create a baseline from the training dataset. Then create a monitoring job in SageMaker Model Monitor. — Build and validate the baseline, then configure scheduled Model Monitor comparisons on captured production data. For actual predictive performance drift, also capture ground truth and use model-quality monitoring.

C. Create a baseline by using a built-in rule in SageMaker Clarify. Monitor the drift in Amazon CloudWatch. — Clarify addresses bias and feature attribution, and a generic 'built-in rule' does not establish the requested production data-quality baseline and schedule.

D. Retrain the model on new data. Compare the retrained model's performance to the original model’s performance. — Comparing one retrained model with the original is a point-in-time evaluation. It does not create ongoing detection of future drift.

text: HOTSPOT - A company stores historical data in .csv files in Amazon S3. Only some of the rows and columns in the .csv files are populated. The columns are not labeled. An ML engineer needs to prepare and store the data so that the company can use the data to train ML models. Select and order the correct steps from the following list to perform this task. Each step should be selected one time or not at all. (Select and order three.) 1. Create an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job for data cleaning and feature engineering. 2. Store the resulting data back in Amazon S3. 3. Use Amazon Athena to infer the schemas and available columns. 4. Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schemas and available columns. 5. Use AWS Glue DataBrew for data cleaning and feature engineering.

choices.A: Step 1: Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 2: Use Amazon Athena to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 3: Create an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job for data cleaning and feature engineering.
choices.B: Step 1: Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 2: Use AWS Glue DataBrew for data cleaning and feature engineering. Step 3: Use Amazon Athena to infer the schemas and available columns.
choices.C: Step 1: Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 2: Create an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job for data cleaning and feature engineering. Step 3: Store the resulting data back in Amazon S3.
choices.D: Step 1: Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 2: Store the resulting data back in Amazon S3. Step 3: Use Amazon Athena to infer the schemas and available columns.
choices.E: Step 1: Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 2: Use AWS Glue DataBrew for data cleaning and feature engineering. Step 3: Store the resulting data back in Amazon S3.
choices.F: Step 1: Create an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job for data cleaning and feature engineering. Step 2: Use AWS Glue DataBrew for data cleaning and feature engineering. Step 3: Store the resulting data back in Amazon S3.

- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: batch
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: A preparation workflow first discovers structure, then cleans and engineers features, and finally persists the prepared dataset for training.

A. Step 1: Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 2: Use Amazon Athena to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 3: Create an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job for data cleaning and feature engineering. — The second schema step is redundant, batch transform is a prediction service rather than the designated preparation tool, and prepared output is not stored.

B. Step 1: Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 2: Use AWS Glue DataBrew for data cleaning and feature engineering. Step 3: Use Amazon Athena to infer the schemas and available columns. — The first two steps are appropriate, but the final step should save the transformed dataset rather than perform another schema discovery operation.

C. Step 1: Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 2: Create an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job for data cleaning and feature engineering. Step 3: Store the resulting data back in Amazon S3. — Schema discovery and S3 output are appropriate, but batch transform is not the general cleaning and feature engineering service requested here.

D. Step 1: Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 2: Store the resulting data back in Amazon S3. Step 3: Use Amazon Athena to infer the schemas and available columns. — This stores data before defining a cleaning transformation and never performs the necessary preparation.

E. Step 1: Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schemas and available columns. Step 2: Use AWS Glue DataBrew for data cleaning and feature engineering. Step 3: Store the resulting data back in Amazon S3. — Use a Glue crawler to infer columns and types, a DataBrew recipe to handle missing values and engineer features, then write the output to S3. Review inferred names and types for the unlabeled sparse source.

F. Step 1: Create an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job for data cleaning and feature engineering. Step 2: Use AWS Glue DataBrew for data cleaning and feature engineering. Step 3: Store the resulting data back in Amazon S3. — This starts with an inference job instead of schema discovery. It does not establish the source structure before preparing the dataset.

text: An ML engineer needs to use Amazon SageMaker Feature Store to create and manage features to train a model. Select and order the steps from the following list to create and use the features in Feature Store. Each step should be selected one time. (Select and order three.) • Access the store to build datasets for training. • Create a feature group. • Ingest the records.

choices.A: Step 1: Access the store to build datasets for training. Step 2: Ingest the records. Step 3: Create a feature group.
choices.B: Step 1: Create a feature group. Step 2: Access the store to build datasets for training. Step 3: Ingest the records.
choices.C: Step 1: Ingest the records. Step 2: Create a feature group. Step 3: Access the store to build datasets for training.
choices.D: Step 1: Create a feature group. Step 2: Ingest the records. Step 3: Access the store to build datasets for training.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: • Create a feature group. • Ingest the records.
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Feature Store requires a feature group definition before records can be ingested and made available for training dataset construction.

A. Step 1: Access the store to build datasets for training. Step 2: Ingest the records. Step 3: Create a feature group. — The store cannot supply these features before the feature group and its records exist; the order is reversed.

B. Step 1: Create a feature group. Step 2: Access the store to build datasets for training. Step 3: Ingest the records. — Creating the group is correct, but a training dataset cannot contain the new records until ingestion completes.

C. Step 1: Ingest the records. Step 2: Create a feature group. Step 3: Access the store to build datasets for training. — Records need a target feature group with defined schema and keys, so ingestion cannot precede group creation.

D. Step 1: Create a feature group. Step 2: Ingest the records. Step 3: Access the store to build datasets for training. — Create the feature group, ingest records with valid identifiers and event times, then query the appropriate store to build the training dataset. Account for offline-store ingestion latency.

text: HOTSPOT - A company wants to host an ML model on Amazon SageMaker. An ML engineer is configuring a continuous integration and continuous delivery (Cl/CD) pipeline in AWS CodePipeline to deploy the model. The pipeline must run automatically when new training data for the model is uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. Select and order the pipeline's correct steps from the following list. Each step should be selected one time or not at all. (Select and order three.) 1. An S3 event notification invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. 2. S3 Lifecycle rule invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. 3. SageMaker retrains the model by using the data in the S3 bucket. 4. The pipeline deploys the model to a SageMaker endpoint. 5. The pipeline deploys the model to SageMaker Model Registry.

choices.A: Step 1: The pipeline deploys the model to SageMaker Model Registry. Step 2: An S3 lifecycle rule invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 3: SageMaker retrains the model by using the data in the S3 bucket.
choices.B: Step 1: An S3 event notification invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 2: S3 Lifecycle rule invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 3: The pipeline deploys the model to a SageMaker endpoint.
choices.C: Step 1: An S3 event notification invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 2: SageMaker retrains the model by using the data in the S3 bucket. Step 3: The pipeline deploys the model to SageMaker Model Registry.
choices.D: Step 1: An S3 event notification invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 2: The pipeline deploys the model to a SageMaker endpoint. Step 3: The pipeline deploys the model to SageMaker Model Registry.
choices.E: Step 1: An S3 event notification invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 2: The pipeline deploys the model to a SageMaker endpoint. Step 3: SageMaker retrains the model by using the data in the S3 bucket.
choices.F: Step 1: An S3 event notification invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 2: SageMaker retrains the model by using the data in the S3 bucket. Step 3: The pipeline deploys the model to a SageMaker endpoint.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: 5. The pipeline deploys the model to SageMaker Model Registry.
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: An event-driven retraining pipeline must receive the data-arrival signal, train a new model, and then deploy an evaluated artifact to a serving endpoint.

A. Step 1: The pipeline deploys the model to SageMaker Model Registry. Step 2: An S3 lifecycle rule invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 3: SageMaker retrains the model by using the data in the S3 bucket. — Model Registry registration is not hosting, and S3 Lifecycle transitions or expires objects rather than triggering this new-data pipeline.

B. Step 1: An S3 event notification invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 2: S3 Lifecycle rule invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 3: The pipeline deploys the model to a SageMaker endpoint. — An S3 Lifecycle rule is not the required event trigger, and this sequence skips training on the uploaded data.

C. Step 1: An S3 event notification invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 2: SageMaker retrains the model by using the data in the S3 bucket. Step 3: The pipeline deploys the model to SageMaker Model Registry. — The trigger and retraining order are appropriate, but registering a model does not host it at an inference endpoint.

D. Step 1: An S3 event notification invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 2: The pipeline deploys the model to a SageMaker endpoint. Step 3: The pipeline deploys the model to SageMaker Model Registry. — This deploys before retraining on the new data and ends with registration rather than the needed training-to-serving sequence.

E. Step 1: An S3 event notification invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 2: The pipeline deploys the model to a SageMaker endpoint. Step 3: SageMaker retrains the model by using the data in the S3 bucket. — Deployment precedes retraining, so the deployed artifact cannot be the one learned from the newly uploaded data.

F. Step 1: An S3 event notification invokes the pipeline when new data is uploaded. Step 2: SageMaker retrains the model by using the data in the S3 bucket. Step 3: The pipeline deploys the model to a SageMaker endpoint. — Route the S3 object-created event through a supported EventBridge or Lambda integration to start CodePipeline, retrain, validate, and deploy to a SageMaker endpoint. An S3 notification does not directly target CodePipeline without that integration.

options.B: An S3 Lifecycle rule is not the required event trigger, and this sequence skips training on the uploaded data.
options.C: The trigger and retraining order are appropriate, but registering a model does not host it at an inference endpoint.

text: HOTSPOT - An ML engineer is working on an ML model to predict the prices of similarly sized homes. The model will base predictions on several features The ML engineer will use the following feature engineering techniques to estimate the prices of the homes: 1. Feature splitting 2. Logarithmic transformation 3. One-hot encoding 4. Standardized distribution Select the correct feature engineering techniques for the following list of features. Each feature engineering technique should be selected one time or not at all (Select three.)

choices.A: City (name): Feature splitting Type_year (type of home and year the home was built): Standardized distribution Size of the building (square feet or square meters): Logarithmic transformation
choices.B: City (name): One-hot encoding Type_year (type of home and year the home was built): Feature splitting Size of the building (square feet or square meters): Logarithmic transformation
choices.C: City (name): One-hot encoding Type_year (type of home and year the home was built): Standardized distribution Size of the building (square feet or square meters): Feature splitting
choices.D: City (name): Logarithmic transformation Type_year (type of home and year the home was built): Feature splitting Size of the building (square feet or square meters): One-hot encoding

hint:

explanation:
Key Concept: Feature engineering should respect data meaning: encode nominal city names, split a field that combines two attributes, and transform positive numerical size only when justified.

A. City (name): Feature splitting Type_year (type of home and year the home was built): Standardized distribution Size of the building (square feet or square meters): Logarithmic transformation — City names are categories rather than a composite field to split, and a combined text type/year cannot be standardized as one numerical value.

B. City (name): One-hot encoding Type_year (type of home and year the home was built): Feature splitting Size of the building (square feet or square meters): Logarithmic transformation — One-hot encode city and split Type_year into home type and year. A log size transform is the plausible numerical transformation among these combinations, but validate its usefulness; similarly sized homes do not automatically imply a skewed size distribution.

C. City (name): One-hot encoding Type_year (type of home and year the home was built): Standardized distribution Size of the building (square feet or square meters): Feature splitting — City encoding is appropriate, but standardizing the combined type/year field and splitting a single numerical size field do not match their meanings.

D. City (name): Logarithmic transformation Type_year (type of home and year the home was built): Feature splitting Size of the building (square feet or square meters): One-hot encoding — A logarithm cannot be applied meaningfully to city names, and one-hot encoding continuous building size would discard its natural numerical structure.

text: A hospital wants to predict patient outcomes for the coming year. An ML engineer must improve several existing ML models that currently perform poorly. Select the correct regularization method from the following list to improve each model. Select each regularization method one time, more than one time, or not at all. (Choose three.) • L1 regularization • L2 regularization • Early stopping

choices.A: A linear regression whose coefficients should shrink but not become zero: L1 regularization A polynomial regression with irrelevant polynomial terms that should be eliminated: L2 regularization A logistic regression with highly correlated features to eliminate redundant predictors: L1 regularization
choices.B: A linear regression whose coefficients should shrink but not become zero: L2 regularization A polynomial regression with irrelevant polynomial terms that should be eliminated: L1 regularization A logistic regression with highly correlated features to eliminate redundant predictors: L2 regularization
choices.C: A linear regression whose coefficients should shrink but not become zero: L2 regularization A polynomial regression with irrelevant polynomial terms that should be eliminated: L1 regularization A logistic regression with highly correlated features to eliminate redundant predictors: L1 regularization
choices.D: A linear regression whose coefficients should shrink but not become zero: L2 regularization A polynomial regression with irrelevant polynomial terms that should be eliminated: L2 regularization A logistic regression with highly correlated features to eliminate redundant predictors: L1 regularization

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: Select each regularization method one time, more than one time, or not at all. (Choose three.) • L1 regularization • L2 regularization • Early stopping
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: L2 shrinks coefficients smoothly, while L1 promotes exact zero coefficients and feature selection. Correlated-feature selection under L1 can be unstable across samples.

A. A linear regression whose coefficients should shrink but not become zero: L1 regularization A polynomial regression with irrelevant polynomial terms that should be eliminated: L2 regularization A logistic regression with highly correlated features to eliminate redundant predictors: L1 regularization — L1 can set coefficients to zero, conflicting with the first requirement. L2 generally does not eliminate the irrelevant polynomial terms in the second task.

B. A linear regression whose coefficients should shrink but not become zero: L2 regularization A polynomial regression with irrelevant polynomial terms that should be eliminated: L1 regularization A logistic regression with highly correlated features to eliminate redundant predictors: L2 regularization — The first two assignments are correct, but L2 tends to retain correlated predictors with shrunken weights rather than eliminate redundant ones.

C. A linear regression whose coefficients should shrink but not become zero: L2 regularization A polynomial regression with irrelevant polynomial terms that should be eliminated: L1 regularization A logistic regression with highly correlated features to eliminate redundant predictors: L1 regularization — Use L2 for shrinkage without intentional sparsity, L1 to eliminate irrelevant polynomial terms, and L1 for sparse selection among redundant logistic-regression predictors. Check selection stability with correlated features.

D. A linear regression whose coefficients should shrink but not become zero: L2 regularization A polynomial regression with irrelevant polynomial terms that should be eliminated: L2 regularization A logistic regression with highly correlated features to eliminate redundant predictors: L1 regularization — The first and third assignments fit, but L2 is not the penalty that explicitly promotes removing polynomial terms by setting their coefficients to zero.

text: An ML engineer needs to use Amazon SageMaker hyperparameter tuning to reduce the training time for an ML model. Select and order the correct steps from the following list to meet this requirement. Each step should be selected one time or not at all. (Select and order three.) • Choose Bayesian optimization and increase the number of parameters. • Choose Hyperband tuning and decrease the number of parameters. • Choose random search and use a random seed of -1. • Deploy the model to a SageMaker endpoint. • Evaluate the change in training time. • Retrain the model.

choices.A: Step 1: Choose Bayesian optimization and increase the number of parameters. Step 2: Retrain the model. Step 3: Evaluate the change in training time.
choices.B: Step 1: Choose random search and use a random seed of -1. Step 2: Retrain the model. Step 3: Evaluate the change in training time.
choices.C: Step 1: Choose Hyperband tuning and decrease the number of parameters. Step 2: Retrain the model. Step 3: Evaluate the change in training time.
choices.D: Step 1: Choose Hyperband tuning and decrease the number of parameters. Step 2: Deploy the model to a SageMaker endpoint. Step 3: Evaluate the change in training time.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: • Evaluate the change in training time. • Retrain the model.
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Hyperband saves tuning resources by stopping unpromising iterative trials early. Measuring the resulting training time requires running the candidate configuration before deployment.

A. Step 1: Choose Bayesian optimization and increase the number of parameters. Step 2: Retrain the model. Step 3: Evaluate the change in training time. — Increasing the number of tuned parameters expands the search problem. Bayesian optimization does not guarantee a faster individual training run.

B. Step 1: Choose random search and use a random seed of -1. Step 2: Retrain the model. Step 3: Evaluate the change in training time. — A random seed does not provide a speed optimization, and the SageMaker tuning RandomSeed parameter requires a nonnegative value, so -1 is invalid.

C. Step 1: Choose Hyperband tuning and decrease the number of parameters. Step 2: Retrain the model. Step 3: Evaluate the change in training time. — Use Hyperband for a supported iterative algorithm, focus the search on relevant parameters, run training, and compare elapsed time and quality. Hyperband reduces wasted tuning work; it does not guarantee that the final selected model trains faster.

D. Step 1: Choose Hyperband tuning and decrease the number of parameters. Step 2: Deploy the model to a SageMaker endpoint. Step 3: Evaluate the change in training time. — Deploying a model does not run the training experiment needed to measure training-time improvement. Retraining and evaluation must precede that decision.

Tag model packages and use model package groups that include container images for training and deployment: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) Store predefined language packages, kernels, and relevant dependencies: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) Organize models and their images into model groups for better discoverability: SageMaker Model Registry Pull built-in SageMaker AI images for model training: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) — The first mapping is wrong: model package groups belong to Model Registry, not ECR. The other three mappings are appropriate.

B. Tag model packages and use model package groups that include container images for training and deployment: SageMaker Model Registry Store predefined language packages, kernels, and relevant dependencies: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) Organize models and their images into model groups for better discoverability: SageMaker Model Registry Pull built-in SageMaker AI images for model training: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) — Use Model Registry for tagged model versions and model groups, and ECR for containerized dependencies and built-in training images. Registry packages reference container images; they do not replace ECR image storage.

C. Tag model packages and use model package groups that include container images for training and deployment: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) Store predefined language packages, kernels, and relevant dependencies: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) Organize models and their images into model groups for better discoverability: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) Pull built-in SageMaker AI images for model training: SageMaker Model Registry — ECR does not provide SageMaker model package groups, and Model Registry is not the image repository from which built-in containers are pulled.

D.
