text: A company needs to combine data from multiple sources. The company must use Amazon Redshift Serverless to query an AWS Glue Data Catalog database and underlying data that is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. Select and order the correct steps from the following list to meet these requirements. Select each step one time or not at all. (Select and order three.) • Attach the IAM role to the Redshift cluster. • Attach the IAM role to the Redshift namespace. • Create an external database in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog schema. • Create an external schema in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog database. • Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access only the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. • Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access the Data Catalog and the S3 bucket that contains underlying data

choices.A: Step 1: Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access the Data Catalog and the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. Step 2: Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access only the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. Step 3: Create an external schema in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog database.
choices.B: Step 1: Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access the Data Catalog and the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. Step 2: Attach the IAM role to the Redshift namespace. Step 3: Create an external schema in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog database.
choices.C: Step 1: Create an external schema in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog database. Step 2: Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access only the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. Step 3: Create an external schema in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog database.
choices.D: Step 1: Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access the Data Catalog and the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. Step 2: Attach the IAM role to the Redshift cluster. Step 3: Create an external schema in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog database.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: • Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access only the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. • Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access the Data Catalog and the S3 bucket that contains underlying data
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: Serverless
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Redshift Serverless associates IAM roles with a namespace. An external schema maps a Glue catalog database into the Redshift SQL environment.

A. Step 1: Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access the Data Catalog and the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. Step 2: Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access only the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. Step 3: Create an external schema in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog database. — Creating a second S3-only role does not associate the required role with the namespace and leaves catalog authorization incomplete.

B. Step 1: Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access the Data Catalog and the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. Step 2: Attach the IAM role to the Redshift namespace. Step 3: Create an external schema in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog database. — Create a role with appropriate Glue catalog and S3 access, associate it with the serverless namespace, then create the external schema referencing the catalog database. Add KMS or Lake Formation permissions when applicable.

C. Step 1: Create an external schema in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog database. Step 2: Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access only the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. Step 3: Create an external schema in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog database. — The sequence tries to create the external schema before establishing access, repeats that step, and never grants or associates the complete required role.

D. Step 1: Create an IAM role for Amazon Redshift to use to access the Data Catalog and the S3 bucket that contains underlying data. Step 2: Attach the IAM role to the Redshift cluster. Step 3: Create an external schema in Amazon Redshift to point to the Data Catalog database. — A provisioned Redshift cluster can have an attached role, but this scenario uses Serverless, where the role is associated with the namespace.

options.A: Creating a second S3-only role does not associate the required role with the namespace and leaves catalog authorization incomplete.
options.B: Create a role with appropriate Glue catalog and S3 access, associate it with the serverless namespace, then create the external schema referencing the catalog database. Add KMS or Lake Formation permissions when applicable.
options.C: The sequence tries to create the external schema before establishing access, repeats that step, and never grants or associates the complete required role.

text: An ML engineer needs to automate the rebuild and redeployment of an ML model. Updates will occur when changes are made to the model’s code base. The ML engineer must use AWS services to con gure a continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline for the rebuild and redeployment. Select and order the steps from the following list to con gure the CI/CD pipeline. Each step should be selected one time. (Select and order three.) • Invoke Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to run all steps required for model training and deployment. • Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. Build and test containers in AWS CodeBuild. • Create a Git source code repository.

choices.A: Step 1: Create a Git source code repository. Step 2: Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. Build and test containers in AWS CodeBuild. Step 3: Invoke Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to run all steps required for model training and deployment.
choices.B: Step 1: Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. Build and test containers in AWS CodeBuild. Step 2: Create a Git source code repository. Step 3: Invoke Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to run all steps required for model training and deployment.
choices.C: Step 1: Invoke Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to run all steps required for model training and deployment. Step 2: Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. Build and test containers in AWS CodeBuild. Step 3: Create a Git source code repository.
choices.D: Step 1: Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. Build and test containers in AWS CodeBuild. Step 2: Invoke Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to run all steps required for model training and deployment. Step 3: Create a Git source code repository.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: Build and test containers in AWS CodeBuild. • Create a Git source code repository.
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: A source-controlled CI/CD workflow builds and tests code changes before invoking model training and controlled deployment stages.

A. Step 1: Create a Git source code repository. Step 2: Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. Build and test containers in AWS CodeBuild. Step 3: Invoke Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to run all steps required for model training and deployment. — Create the source repository, configure CodePipeline and CodeBuild to react to changes and validate containers, then invoke the SageMaker workflow with explicit training, evaluation, and deployment integration.

B. Step 1: Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. Build and test containers in AWS CodeBuild. Step 2: Create a Git source code repository. Step 3: Invoke Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to run all steps required for model training and deployment. — The pipeline's source and change trigger depend on the repository. Creating the repository after configuring that source reverses the intended setup dependency.

C. Step 1: Invoke Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to run all steps required for model training and deployment. Step 2: Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. Build and test containers in AWS CodeBuild. Step 3: Create a Git source code repository. — This invokes the ML workflow before establishing the source repository and build/test stages that should supply its validated code.

D. Step 1: Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. Build and test containers in AWS CodeBuild. Step 2: Invoke Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to run all steps required for model training and deployment. Step 3: Create a Git source code repository. — The repository appears last, so the described pipeline cannot yet be driven by its code changes.

text: A company is using Amazon SageMaker to deploy a new version of its ML model. Select the correct SageMaker traffic shifting strategy from the following list for each use case. Each traffic shifting strategy should be selected one time. (Choose three.) • All at once traffic shifting • Canary traffic shifting • Linear traffic shifting

choices.A: Shift traffic in two steps to validate the new model version: All at once traffic shifting Shift traffic to the new model version in the shortest amount of time: Canary traffic shifting Incrementally shift traffic to the new model version over time: Linear traffic shifting
choices.B: Shift traffic in two steps to validate the new model version: Linear traffic shifting Shift traffic to the new model version in the shortest amount of time: All at once traffic shifting Incrementally shift traffic to the new model version over time: Canary traffic shifting
choices.C: Shift traffic in two steps to validate the new model version: Canary traffic shifting Shift traffic to the new model version in the shortest amount of time: All at once traffic shifting Incrementally shift traffic to the new model version over time: Linear traffic shifting
choices.D: Shift traffic in two steps to validate the new model version: Canary traffic shifting Shift traffic to the new model version in the shortest amount of time: Linear traffic shifting Incrementally shift traffic to the new model version over time: All at once traffic shifting

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: Each traffic shifting strategy should be selected one time. (Choose three.) • All at once traffic shifting • Canary traffic shifting • Linear traffic shifting
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: All-at-once moves traffic in one step, canary first tests a small portion before the remainder, and linear shifts equal increments over time.

A. Shift traffic in two steps to validate the new model version: All at once traffic shifting Shift traffic to the new model version in the shortest amount of time: Canary traffic shifting Incrementally shift traffic to the new model version over time: Linear traffic shifting — All-at-once does not provide the two-stage canary validation, and canary is not the shortest one-step traffic shift.

B. Shift traffic in two steps to validate the new model version: Linear traffic shifting Shift traffic to the new model version in the shortest amount of time: All at once traffic shifting Incrementally shift traffic to the new model version over time: Canary traffic shifting — Linear shifting is incremental rather than the specific two-step canary pattern. Canary is not the repeated equal-increment strategy.

C. Shift traffic in two steps to validate the new model version: Canary traffic shifting Shift traffic to the new model version in the shortest amount of time: All at once traffic shifting Incrementally shift traffic to the new model version over time: Linear traffic shifting — Canary fits two-stage validation, all-at-once completes traffic shifting fastest after the new fleet is ready, and linear provides gradual increments.

D. Shift traffic in two steps to validate the new model version: Canary traffic shifting Shift traffic to the new model version in the shortest amount of time: Linear traffic shifting Incrementally shift traffic to the new model version over time: All at once traffic shifting — The canary mapping is correct, but linear and all-at-once are reversed for fastest versus incremental traffic movement.

text: An ML engineer needs to use Amazon SageMaker to develop an ML solution for a company. The solution will use streaming video from cameras to count the number of people who walk past the company’s store every day. Select and order the steps from the following list to implement the first version of the algorithm. Each step should be selected one time. (Select and order three.) • Choose a built-in algorithm or pre-trained model. • Decide the data input format and apply data augmentation if necessary. • Determine if the challenge is a classification, detection, or segmentation problem.

choices.A: Step 1: Determine if the challenge is a classification, detection, or segmentation problem. Step 2: Decide the data input format and apply data augmentation if necessary. Step 3: Choose a built-in algorithm or pre-trained model.
choices.B: Step 1: Decide the data input format and apply data augmentation if necessary. Step 2: Choose a built-in algorithm or pre-trained model. Step 3: Determine if the challenge is a classification, detection, or segmentation problem.
choices.C: Step 1: Choose a built-in algorithm or pre-trained model. Step 2: Determine if the challenge is a classification, detection, or segmentation problem. Step 3: Decide the data input format and apply data augmentation if necessary.
choices.D: Step 1: Determine if the challenge is a classification, detection, or segmentation problem. Step 2: Choose a built-in algorithm or pre-trained model. Step 3: Decide the data input format and apply data augmentation if necessary.

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: • Decide the data input format and apply data augmentation if necessary. • Determine if the challenge is a classification, detection, or segmentation problem.
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: First define the computer vision task, then choose a suitable model, and prepare inputs according to that model's requirements. Counting unique passers-by also needs tracking logic.

A. Step 1: Determine if the challenge is a classification, detection, or segmentation problem. Step 2: Decide the data input format and apply data augmentation if necessary. Step 3: Choose a built-in algorithm or pre-trained model. — The task is correctly identified first, but committing to a final training input format before selecting the model can lead to incompatible data preparation.

B. Step 1: Decide the data input format and apply data augmentation if necessary. Step 2: Choose a built-in algorithm or pre-trained model. Step 3: Determine if the challenge is a classification, detection, or segmentation problem. — Preparing data and choosing a model before defining the task risks optimizing for the wrong output, such as image classification instead of object detection.

C. Step 1: Choose a built-in algorithm or pre-trained model. Step 2: Determine if the challenge is a classification, detection, or segmentation problem. Step 3: Decide the data input format and apply data augmentation if necessary. — Selecting an algorithm before determining whether the task requires detection, segmentation, or classification reverses the key design dependency.

D. Step 1: Determine if the challenge is a classification, detection, or segmentation problem. Step 2: Choose a built-in algorithm or pre-trained model. Step 3: Decide the data input format and apply data augmentation if necessary. — Identify the task, choose an appropriate built-in or pretrained model, and then prepare its required input format and valid augmentations. Add tracking or line-crossing rules to avoid counting the same person in successive frames.

options.B: Preparing data and choosing a model before defining the task risks optimizing for the wrong output, such as image classification instead of object detection.

Select the correct AWS service from the following list to perform each task on the data. Each service should be selected one time or not at all. (Select three.) 1. Amazon Athena 2. AWS Glue 3. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams 4. Amazon S3

choices.A: Query the data for exploration and analysis: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Store the data: Amazon S3 Transform the data: AWS Glue
choices.B: Query the data for exploration and analysis: Amazon Athena Store the data: Amazon S3 Transform the data: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
choices.C: Query the data for exploration and analysis: Amazon Athena Store the data: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Transform the data: AWS Glue
choices.D: Query the data for exploration and analysis: Amazon Athena Store the data: AWS Glue Transform the data: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
choices.E: Query the data for exploration and analysis: AWS Glue Store the data: Amazon S3 Transform the data: Amazon Athena
choices.F: Query the data for exploration and analysis: Amazon Athena Store the data: Amazon S3 Transform the data: AWS Glue

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams 4. Amazon S3
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: A common data-lake workflow uses S3 for durable storage, Athena for interactive SQL exploration, and Glue for managed data preparation.

A. Query the data for exploration and analysis: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Store the data: Amazon S3 Transform the data: AWS Glue — Kinesis Data Streams ingests and retains streaming records; it is not an interactive SQL query engine for historical S3 data.

B. Query the data for exploration and analysis: Amazon Athena Store the data: Amazon S3 Transform the data: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams — Athena and S3 fit the first two tasks, but Kinesis Data Streams is not the general ETL transformation engine.

C. Query the data for exploration and analysis: Amazon Athena Store the data: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Transform the data: AWS Glue — Athena and Glue fit their tasks, but a stream is not the intended durable historical object store.

D. Query the data for exploration and analysis: Amazon Athena Store the data: AWS Glue Transform the data: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams — Glue is not the primary object storage service, and Kinesis Data Streams does not replace the ETL transformation service.

E. Query the data for exploration and analysis: AWS Glue Store the data: Amazon S3 Transform the data: Amazon Athena — Glue can run analysis code and Athena can express transformations in SQL, but this reverses the intended dedicated interactive-query and managed-ETL roles.

F. Query the data for exploration and analysis: Amazon Athena Store the data: Amazon S3 Transform the data: AWS Glue — Query historical data with Athena, store it in S3, and use Glue jobs to clean, aggregate, and engineer the training features.

text: A global e-commerce company has developed a custom sentiment analysis model using Amazon Comprehend in Account A within the us-west-2 Region. The company now needs to copy the model to Account B, which handles customer service operations, so that the model can be used to analyze customer feedback. The solution must ensure secure and efficient transfer of the model with minimal development effort. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use the Amazon Comprehend ImportModel API operation in Account B to securely import the sentiment analysis model from Account A by configuring a resource based IAM policy in account A
choices.B: Leverage AWS Glue Data Catalog to register the model metadata in Account A and enable cross-account sharing with Account B. Use the Comprehend console in Account B to access the model
choices.C: Manually download the model artifacts from Amazon S3 in Account A and upload them to an S3 bucket in Account B. Use a custom script to recreate the model in Account B
choices.D: Use the Amazon Comprehend ImportModel API operation in Account B to securely import the sentiment analysis model from Account A by configuring a resource based IAM policy in account B

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The solution must ensure secure and efficient transfer of the model with minimal development effort. Which solution will meet these requirements?
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Comprehend can share a supported custom classifier or entity recognizer through a resource policy on the source model, then copy it with ImportModel in the destination account.

A. Use the Amazon Comprehend ImportModel API operation in Account B to securely import the sentiment analysis model from Account A by configuring a resource based IAM policy in account A — Grant Account B access through the model resource policy in Account A, then call ImportModel in Account B in the supported Region. For this scenario, sentiment must be implemented as a custom classifier; the managed DetectSentiment model is not a customer-owned model to copy.

B. Leverage AWS Glue Data Catalog to register the model metadata in Account A and enable cross-account sharing with Account B. Use the Comprehend console in Account B to access the model — Glue Data Catalog shares data metadata. It does not transfer a Comprehend custom model or authorize its import.

C. Manually download the model artifacts from Amazon S3 in Account A and upload them to an S3 bucket in Account B. Use a custom script to recreate the model in Account B — Comprehend does not provide this as a generic downloadable-artifact recreation workflow. Manual retraining would add effort compared with the supported import operation.

D. Use the Amazon Comprehend ImportModel API operation in Account B to securely import the sentiment analysis model from Account A by configuring a resource based IAM policy in account B — The destination account cannot grant itself access to a model owned by Account A. The source owner must authorize access on the source model.

options.B: Glue Data Catalog shares data metadata. It does not transfer a Comprehend custom model or authorize its import.

options.D: The destination account cannot grant itself access to a model owned by Account A. The source owner must authorize access on the source model.

text: A financial services company is building a customer churn prediction model on AWS. The dataset includes call logs, customer interaction history, and transactional data from an on-premises PostgreSQL database. The call logs and interaction history are stored in Amazon S3, while the PostgreSQL tables remain on-premises. The data science team needs to aggregate and preprocess data from these various sources to ensure it is ready for machine learning model training. They must also resolve challenges such as feature inconsistencies and ensure schema alignment across the data sources. Which AWS service or feature can efficiently connect and aggregate the data from these sources?

text: A fintech company is developing an AI-driven fraud detection system using Amazon SageMaker. The system must provide end-to-end ML capabilities, including data preprocessing, model training, versioned model storage, deployment, and monitoring. Customer transaction data is stored securely in Amazon S3. The company requires the following: Secure access to training data for different ML workflows to ensure data isolation. A centralized model registry to manage model versions and deployments with minimal operational overhead. What is the most appropriate approach to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Use Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) to store model artifacts and versions
choices.B: Use Amazon S3 versioning to track model artifacts and manage deployments manually
choices.C: Use SageMaker Model Registry to manage model versions and associate models with model groups
choices.D: Use unique tags for each model version and use SageMaker Model Registry to manage model deployments

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: A centralized model registry to manage model versions and deployments with minimal operational overhead. What is the most appropriate approach to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

explanation:
Key Concept: Model Registry provides managed model version groups and lifecycle metadata. Training-data isolation must still be enforced independently through IAM, S3, and network controls.

A. Use Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) to store model artifacts and versions — ECR versions container images, but does not by itself manage model packages, approval states, and model version groups.

B. Use Amazon S3 versioning to track model artifacts and manage deployments manually — S3 versioning preserves artifact object versions, but manual deployment and metadata tracking increase operational effort.

C. Use SageMaker Model Registry to manage model versions and associate models with model groups — Register models in model package groups to manage versions and approval metadata with minimal custom infrastructure. Apply workflow-specific execution roles and data access policies separately; registry grouping alone does not isolate training data.

D. Use unique tags for each model version and use SageMaker Model Registry to manage model deployments — Unique tags can aid discovery, but are not needed to reinvent the version numbering and grouping already provided by Model Registry.

text: A retail company has deployed a machine learning (ML) model using Amazon SageMaker to forecast product demand. The model is exposed via a SageMaker endpoint that processes requests from multiple applications. The company needs to record and monitor all API call events made to the endpoint and receive a notification whenever the number of requests exceeds a specific threshold during peak traffic hours. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the API call metrics for the SageMaker endpoint and create an alarm to send notifications through Amazon SNS when the call count breaches the threshold
choices.B: Use SageMaker Model Monitor to capture and analyze endpoint traffic and configure a rule to notify when API calls exceed the specified threshold
choices.C: Use Amazon EventBridge to capture SageMaker API call events and configure a rule to send a notification when the event count breaches the threshold
choices.D: Enable AWS CloudTrail to log all SageMaker API call events and use CloudTrail Insights to send notifications when the API call volume exceeds a threshold

hint:
- Bài toán thực sự đang hỏi: The company needs to record and monitor all API call events made to the endpoint and receive a notification whenever the number of requests exceeds a specific threshold during peak traffic hours. Which solution will meet these requirements?
- Keyword/constraint nên gạch chân: mục tiêu cuối cùng, loại workload, yêu cầu latency/cost/operational effort và phạm vi dữ liệu.
- Cách loại trừ: Xác định dịch vụ hoặc tính năng được AWS thiết kế trực tiếp cho requirement; sau đó loại phương án chỉ technically possible nhưng tăng vận hành, chi phí hoặc không giải quyết đúng mục tiêu.
explanation:
Key Concept: Invocation count metrics and per-call audit records are different outputs. Fixed-volume alerting uses CloudWatch alarms; endpoint invocation auditing requires enabled CloudTrail data events.

A. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the API call metrics for the SageMaker endpoint and create an alarm to send notifications through Amazon SNS when the call count breaches the threshold — CloudWatch invocation metrics and an SNS alarm meet the count-threshold notification requirement. They do not by themselves record every API call event, so the source answer is incomplete for the full wording.

B. Use SageMaker Model Monitor to capture and analyze endpoint traffic and configure a rule to notify when API calls exceed the specified threshold — Model Monitor evaluates captured data and predictions. It is not the API audit trail or simplest request-count alarm service.

C. Use Amazon EventBridge to capture SageMaker API call events and configure a rule to send a notification when the event count breaches the threshold — EventBridge routes matching events, but a rule does not automatically aggregate all calls into a threshold counter or guarantee a complete audit log.

D. Enable AWS CloudTrail to log all SageMaker API call events and use CloudTrail Insights to send notifications when the API call volume exceeds a threshold — CloudTrail can log endpoint invocations when the appropriate data events are enabled. Insights detects unusual API activity rather than implementing the specified fixed request-count threshold; combine auditing with the CloudWatch/SNS portion of A.
notes: Source selects A. CloudWatch and SNS satisfy threshold alerting, but do not record every API event. Enable CloudTrail endpoint data events as well. CloudTrail Insights is not the fixed-count threshold alarm described.

text: Which AWS service is used to store, share and manage inputs to Machine Learning models used during training and inference?

choices.B: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store

choices.D: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth

explanation:
Key Concept: A feature store is a reusable repository of model input features for training and inference, with consistent definitions and access patterns.

A. Amazon SageMaker Clarify — Clarify evaluates bias and explains predictions. It is not the feature repository.

D. Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth — Ground Truth manages data labeling workflows and workforces, not serving shared feature records for inference.

text: A company specializes in providing personalized product recommendations for e-commerce platforms. You’ve been tasked with developing a solution that can quickly generate high-quality product descriptions, tailor marketing copy based on customer preferences, and analyze customer reviews to identify trends in sentiment. Given the scale of data and the need for flexibility in choosing foundational models, you decide to use an AI service that can integrate seamlessly with your existing AWS infrastructure while also offering managed foundational models from third-party providers. Which AWS service would best meet your requirements?

choices.A: Amazon SageMaker
choices.B: Amazon Rekognition
choices.C: Amazon Personalize
choices.D: Amazon Bedrock

D. Amazon Bedrock — Bedrock offers supported foundation models for generating product text, adapting prompts to customer context, and analyzing review sentiment. Select and evaluate the model suited to each task and its current availability.
